title: The Dangerous Appeal of Fake AI Users
intro: Synthetic or “proxy” users let teams simulate research without doing any. The output looks enough like insight to pass. Calabro's test is practical: what would a real person tell you that a model never could?

topics.title: The Dangerous Appeal of Fake AI Users

learn.title: Ten things a proxy user never says
learn.text:
Real sessions produce moments like:

“I gave up halfway through because I got frustrated.”
“I don't know what that button does, so I avoid it.”
“I use this workaround every time because your system is too slow.”
“I didn't even notice that feature until you pointed it out.”
“I thought it worked. Then I realized it didn't.”

These are the unknown unknowns that make or break a project.

try.q: Which statement could only come from a real user?
options: “I use this workaround every time.”
“Users generally prefer simple flows.”
“This feature would likely be valuable.”
“The layout appears clear and modern.”
try.explain: A workaround is lived behaviour. The others are plausible generalities a model can produce.

learn.title: Things people hide
learn.text:
Also on his list:

“I lied in your survey because I thought it would help me finish faster.”
“I feel stupid asking this, but…”
“I clicked that by mistake, but I didn't want to say anything.”
“I had to ask a coworker how to do it.”
“Honestly, I don't trust your product to do this right.”

try.q: A participant says “I clicked that by mistake, but I didn't want to say anything.” What does this show?
options: Real sessions surface behaviour people hide
The participant was poorly recruited
The moderator asked a leading question earlier in the session
The prototype needs higher fidelity
try.explain: Embarrassment and hidden errors only appear with real people.

learn.title: Scaling the decay
learn.text:
Calabro's biggest worry is not that proxy users give PMs a shortcut to their own opinions. It is that **whole teams can build fast on simulated research**.

He traces it to years of speed over quality: trading synthesis for sentiment and pushing researchers out of early stages.

try.q: What does Calabro see as the biggest threat of proxy users?
options: Teams scale up work built on simulated research
AI tools are still too expensive for small product teams
Participants will lose paid research work
PMs will stop attending research sessions
try.explain: They scale the decay of research across entire teams.

test.q: What is a “proxy user” in this article?
options: An AI stand-in for real research participants
A colleague who role-plays a customer during design reviews
A power user who represents a segment
A persona built from interview data
test.explain: It is the synthetic-user idea: talking to a chatbot instead of people.

test.q: Why does synthetic output get accepted?
options: It looks enough like insight to pass
It is statistically more reliable than interviews
It always matches analytics data
Researchers usually recommend it
test.explain: The output is coherent and plausible, which is the danger.

test.q: Which is on Calabro's list of things a proxy user never says?
options: “I had to ask a coworker how to do it.”
“I would rate this four out of five.”
“The onboarding seems well structured.”
“I prefer the second design option.”
test.explain: Asking a coworker is a real workaround in a real setting.

test.q: What do the ten statements have in common?
options: They uncover unknown unknowns
They are all complaints about speed
They come from expert users only
They can be predicted in advance
test.explain: They are the parts of a session that lead to real learning.

test.q: Where does Calabro say the trend comes from?
options: Years of pushing for speed over quality
A long-running shortage of trained UX researchers
Stricter privacy rules on recruiting
Users refusing to join studies
test.explain: PMs didn't set out to break research, but speed-first habits led here.
